method:
Geometry first. I loaded prims.pkl (area upper, x 80.5-106, y 6-26) and dumped every WALL, COL, WIN, WALL-GL, D-JAMB, DOOR, I-DOOR, A-DOOR, FLOOR, HATCH and TREE item with exact coordinates. I then traced each wall line for interruptions: end caps, jamb pieces, door blocks, swing arcs and pocket-door panels. A script listing unconnected wall-line ends found no gap left unexplained.

Each candidate was checked on zoomed renders at a 0.1-0.5 m grid:
- bedroom and south wall: 81-89.5 x 6.5-13 and 81.5-89.5 x 7.2-8.6
- bedroom west and east glazing: 81.3-83.6 x 7.2-12.9 and 87.6-89.8 x 7.3-11.4
- bathroom and corridor: 81.4-89.4 x 12.2-17.2
- dressing room, walk-in closet and doors: 84.5-88.6 x 15.3-19.6 at a 0.1 m grid, and 81.3-89.3 x 17-25.2
- bridge: 87.6-94.2 x 18.2-22.2
- courtyard north and south: 88.2-94.2 x 21-25.5 and 88.2-94.2 x 12.5-19.6
- stair hall: 92.5-102.5 x 20.5-25.3
- void: 92.6-101.6 x 13.9-19.9
- landing: 93-101.5 x 18.4-21.6
- lounge and pocket doors: 99.5-108.5 x 13.8-25.2 and 99.6-103.6 x 15.8-21.8
- south roof: 88-96 x 6.5-14.6 and 95-105.5 x 6.5-14.8

a and b are on the wall centre line, at the wall-end, column or rebate faces, with frames and cladding included. Widths come from exact coordinates.

Window versus glass wall: the section at sheet x 7-45, y 41-63 looks east at the main block's courtyard face at twice plan scale. It shows the stair-hall glazing, the double-height void glazing and the bridge glazing running full height on the upper floor, so those are listed as glass walls. Every other kind was decided from plan cues: balcony and balustrade, planter, gravel roof, layer. A final render with a marker on every opening and glass wall (check_all, check_wing, check_main) showed no unmarked gap, leaf, jamb pair or window.
